newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey says Iraq buffer zone may be part emptied.
newsitem.headline: Turkey says Iraq buffer zone may be part emptied.

text.p: Turkey may clear some settlements from a "buffer zone" it plans to create in northern Iraq to stop infiltrations by separatist Turkish Kurdish rebels, Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller said on Saturday.
"Settlements in the buffer zone to be created may be partially emptied because of the terrorists, but not generally," Ciller was quoted by the state-run Anatolian news agency as saying.

A foreign ministry official said Ankara wanted to empty some border settlements to ensure civilians did not get caught up in fighting or were not able to give refuge or support to the Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) guerrillas. He did not say how they could be emptied or how many settlements Ciller was taking about.

After U.S. missile attacks last week on southern Iraq in retaliation against Baghdad for sending troops into Kurdish areas of northern Iraq, Turkey said it planned to set up a buffer zone against attacks from the separatist PKK, which uses bases in the region to stage attacks in Turkey.
The United States has said it understands Turkey's reasons for establishing a security zone in Iraq as long as it is temporary and involves no permanent stationing of troops.
But France, Russia and neighbour Syria have opposed the plan. Baghdad has said it would be "unacceptable".
